question: Can weight-only INT8 for the 48 static Transformer linear matrices preserve P1 R1 quality and produce enough same-device full-chain speedup without quantizing activations, Softmax, normalization, residuals, or the depth head?
numbering_note: A5_FULL_IMAGE_INT8 remains forbidden in the parent protocol; A5S is a distinct selective sub-arm and does not authorize full-image INT8

profile_basis.expected_risk: quality risk is lower than activation quantization, but attainable latency gain may be below the frozen 1.15x full-chain gate

precision_contract.quantized_tensors: exactly the 48 second-input static weights of qkv, projection, fc1, and fc2 MatMul nodes across Transformer blocks 0 through 11
precision_contract.weight_encoding: symmetric signed INT8, zero point 0, per-output-channel scale on ONNX axis 1
precision_contract.reason_no_calibration: only immutable static weights are encoded; no activation encoding is generated
precision_contract.conversion_adaptation_gate: converted DLC must retain exactly the intended 48 INT8 weight encodings and FP16 graph IO; silent promotion to FP16 or propagation into activations is a conversion failure

execution_order: convert and inspect DLC precision before any P1 candidate cache
if and only if the precision contract passes, materialize all 120 P1 outputs without opening sensor truth
lock candidate cache SHA-256 and run P1 R1 once
only after quality pass, generate an SM8650 cached context and run fixed-APK same-device output parity, P95, full-chain, and sustained checks

quality_gate.absolute_task_metrics: reported separately and not rescued by precision parity

performance_gate.rule: a quality-passing arm below either 1.15x full-chain speedup or 8 Hz cannot fill the high-frequency student role

forbidden: quantize activations, Softmax, LayerNorm, residuals, graph IO, patch embedding, or depth head in this arm
add calibration data or switch per-channel axis after conversion or P1 output
try multiple layer subsets, axes, bitwidths, schemes, or converter flags and select by P1
profile a quality-failed candidate and use speed to rescue it
treat weight parity, DLC creation, HTP execution, or consumed P1 evidence as product or safety authority
